content.text: {"eligibility": "include", "criterion": "IC", "side_list": "none", "reason": "Trains and evaluates an LLM (Qwen3-8B with SFT and execution-aware RL) generating HIP/Triton kernels, reporting quantitative speedup (efficiency) alongside correctness, so EC5 does not apply.", "nf_outcomes_found": "Kernel speedup (efficiency) over PyTorch or input-kernel baselines for LLM-generated kernels: Speed@10 1.14× (HIP-to-HIP, Table 3); Speed 1.46× (TritonBench-G, Table 4); Speed 1.61× (ROCmBench, Table 5); latency-profiled speedups in the case studies."}

{"eligibility": "include", "criterion": "IC", "side_list": "none", "reason": "Proposes an RL/SFT technique (GRPO with simulation reward) applied to an LLM generating C++ code, and reports quantitative energy (CARET, ERR, energy reduction) outcomes for generated code.", "nf_outcomes_found": "CARET 12.63% (energy-reduction metric, correctness-adjusted) vs 4.45% SFT; mean ERR on valid outputs 34.20%; Beat-GT 58.4% of valid outputs beating human reference energy; compile rate 81.7%; runtime speedups (e.g., 1.64x) for examples"}

{"eligibility": "include", "criterion": "IC", "side_list": "none", "reason": "The JevVibe repair agent applies a diagnosis-guided post-generation repair to Qwen2.5-Coder-32B code and reports security pass rate, fixes and regressions measured by CyberSecEval's insecure-code detector.", "nf_outcomes_found": "Security pass rate on LLM-generated code rises from 63.5% (baseline) to 70.7% with Jev-guided repair vs 66.1% with LLM-guided repair; fixes 228 vs 129 and regressions 89 vs 79 (1,916 examples)."}

{"eligibility": "include", "criterion": "IC", "side_list": "none", "reason": "Evaluates 21 prompting strategies (a prompt-level technique) on LLM-generated Python and C++ code and reports quantitative energy-consumption reductions (up to 25% Python, 17% C++), satisfying IC1-IC4.", "nf_outcomes_found": "Energy consumption of LLM-generated Python and C++ code measured via perf: average relative energy change vs. baseline prompt, e.g., Prompt 20 −25% (Python), Prompt 13 −17% (C++); per-model reductions up to 50% (Granite-4.0-H-Small Python) and 57% (Granite C++)."}

{"eligibility": "include", "criterion": "IC", "side_list": "none", "reason": "Applies DPO and BoNBoN alignment to code LLMs and reports quantitative CODAL scores for readability, style, and complexity/efficiency of the generated code, with full paper.", "nf_outcomes_found": "CODAL 0-10 LLM-judge scores for code readability (NF2), coding style (NF4), and complexity/efficiency (NF3) of generated code. Relative gains reported, e.g., CodeLlama-7b avg +75% (0.48→0.84), deepseek-coder-7b +27.8%, Qwen2.5-Coder-7B +15.7%. EvalPerf efficiency is also reported (F3), though labelled functional."}

{"eligibility": "uncertain", "criterion": "IC3", "side_list": "none", "reason": "LLM agents edit VPR C++ source (IC1, IC2 met), and tool runtime of the evolved code is reported, but the main outcomes are circuit QoR (CPD, WL), so whether IC3 holds is unclear.", "nf_outcomes_found": "Per-seed VPR tool runtime (RT) of LLM-evolved VPR versus stock VPR, up to 79.3% reduction, and versus AutoTuner, up to 7.8%; also CPD and routed wirelength of the resulting designs, which are circuit QoR rather than code quality."}

{"eligibility": "uncertain", "criterion": "IC3", "side_list": "correctness-only", "reason": "Primary outcomes are semantic correctness and code similarity. Robustness outcomes (runtime-error avoidance of added hardening/exception handling, 40-45%) may or may not count as NF quality.", "nf_outcomes_found": "Runtime-error avoidance from added Code Hardening (40.3% of 188) and Exception Handling (44.8% of 106) changes; category counts for Refactoring/Code Hardening; similarity to human code (PDG/AST/CodeBLEU), which is not an NF measure."}

{"eligibility": "include", "criterion": "IC", "side_list": "none", "reason": "Evaluates model editing and a post-edit refinement (SafeEdit) on LLM-generated code, with quantitative CodeQL-based security ratios and inference/training latency reported for that code.", "nf_outcomes_found": "Security ratio (CodeQL-based % secure completions) on seen CWEs (e.g., DINM +11.27% avg over vanilla, UltraEdit +6.54%, CoSec +1.46%), unseen-CWE security ratios, CodeGuard+ secure-pass@1 (e.g., 36.57 to 50.34 avg), and efficiency (hardening time and per-query latency in seconds, CoSec 1.4–3.2x inference overhead)."}

{"eligibility": "include", "criterion": "IC", "side_list": "none", "reason": "Proposes an inference-time multi-agent technique (MKEvolve) generating Triton kernels with LLMs and reports runtime speedup vs torch.compile (Fast0.5/1/2), an efficiency NF outcome.", "nf_outcomes_found": "Runtime efficiency of LLM-generated Triton kernels: Fast_p speedup metrics vs torch.compile (e.g., Fast1 0.49 vs 0.36 beam search, Claude 4.5 Opus L2); also end-to-end speedups (e.g., 1.8x MobileNetV1, 10.7x-44.3x FlashInfer tasks)."}

{"eligibility": "include", "criterion": "IC", "side_list": "none", "reason": "Applies a prompt-based distillation technique (UTT Primer) to LLM-generated CUDA kernels on KernelBench and reports Fast1, the fraction of kernels that are correct and faster than the PyTorch reference (an efficiency outcome).", "nf_outcomes_found": "KernelBench Fast1@5 (fraction of problems with at least one correct sample that is faster than the PyTorch reference), e.g., Pro→Flash 9% to 35%, Pro→Qwen 9.2% to 50.0% accuracy with Fast1 12 to 32; runtime measured on an RTX A6000."}

{"eligibility": "include", "criterion": "IC", "side_list": "none", "reason": "RPG is a decoding intervention on CodeLlama; it reports TR-N/TR-S statement and n-gram repetition (redundancy) of LLM-generated code, plus generation length and time, beyond correctness and compilability.", "nf_outcomes_found": "TR-N and TR-S (structural/content repetition rates of generated code, lower is better), GenLen and Time (generation length and cost); EGP and CCP are termination and compilability measures, not NF."}

{"eligibility": "include", "criterion": "IC", "side_list": "none", "reason": "Proposes a prompt/rule-evolution technique for LLM coding agents and reports quantitative NF outcomes on generated code: code length, cyclomatic complexity, Halstead volume, maintainability index, duplication, and docstring rate (Appendix D).", "nf_outcomes_found": "Code lines and characters (length/conciseness), token usage and generation time (cost); Appendix D: cyclomatic complexity 5.37→3.95, Halstead volume 53.0→28.0, maintainability index 85.1→78.3, duplicated-block ratio 0.10%→0.00%, docstring rate 47%→1%."}

{"eligibility": "include", "criterion": "IC", "side_list": "none", "reason": "Systematically perturbs prompts (removing syntactic constituents) for open LLMs and measures CodeQL vulnerability rates of the generated code, a quantitative security outcome on LLM-generated code.", "nf_outcomes_found": "CodeQL vulnerability rates for LLM-generated code per model and language (e.g., Python baseline 40.66% vs. permutations up to ~100% for late-sentence removals), plus risk ratios for constituent types, positions and granularities."}

{"eligibility": "uncertain", "criterion": "IC1", "side_list": "context", "reason": "The main contribution is a detection/admission pipeline evaluated mostly on constructed mutants; the LLM-generated stratum mostly measures unmodified outputs, and the post-hoc bounded repair targets interface and functional yield, not NF quality.", "nf_outcomes_found": "On generated candidates: family-level defect counts (privacy 112, lifecycle 85, provenance 46, authority 4, reliability 3 among 112 repaired P0-passing candidates); P0–P4 vs P0–P2 detection (100% vs 13.4%) on that subset; 0/600 unmodified generations passed P0 or full conformance; security-family recall reported only for mutants."}

{"eligibility": "include", "criterion": "IC", "side_list": "none", "reason": "Evaluates security context and specification interventions (P0–P3, D0–D2, repair rounds, spec edits) on LLM-written DNS, reassembly, HTTP and firewall programs, with attack success rate as the outcome.", "nf_outcomes_found": "Attack success rate (ASR) of LLM-written D-mode programs against security cases: median 0–4% on reassembly, HTTP and firewall at D2, and about 15% on DNS (range 11–23%); 0x20 check ASR fell from 100% to 34% after a spec change."}

{"eligibility": "uncertain", "criterion": "IC3", "side_list": "none", "reason": "Technique (RL post-training) and LLM-edited code are clear, but the quantitative outcome is edit size (Levenshtein distance), which is a maintainability-related proxy rather than a clear readability, efficiency, or security measure.", "nf_outcomes_found": "Character- and line-level Levenshtein edit distance of LLM edits to LLM-authored Rust functions (reported as reduced excessive editing, framed as reviewer burden); build and test pass rates are correctness co-outcomes."}

{"eligibility": "include", "criterion": "IC", "side_list": "none", "reason": "Proposes a multi-agent technique for LLM code generation and evaluates it with quantitative security outcomes (Sec@1, F&S@1) on CWEval and BaxBench, beyond correctness alone.", "nf_outcomes_found": "CWEval Sec@1 for GPT-4o rises from 53.91% (Direct) to 79.31% (MACGen); F&S@1 70.59%. BaxBench GPT-4o F&S@1 21.17% to 31.12%. Security (CWE) outcomes are reported for LLM-generated code."}

{"eligibility": "include", "criterion": "IC", "side_list": "none", "reason": "Proposes an inference-time in-stream self-repair technique for LLM code generation and reports quantitative security outcomes (insecure delivery rates, Secure & Func. rates) for the generated code.", "nf_outcomes_found": "Insecure & Func. deliveries fall from 79.0-92.3% (RAW) to at most 3.1% with SecReason; Secure & Func. rises from below 15% to 72.8-98.1%; mean tokens per run compared with post-hoc repair (SecReason 4,381-6,361 vs 5,144-15,491 for Post-Hoc Repair); false-positive token overhead of 0.9x-1.6x."}

{"eligibility": "uncertain", "criterion": "EC5", "side_list": "correctness-only", "reason": "The only outcome is crate hallucination rate (non-existent crate references), framed as security risk but not a vulnerability, readability, or efficiency measure; the paper says it does not measure exploitability.", "nf_outcomes_found": "none (crate hallucination rate, CHR, of LLM-generated Rust code: 22.23% overall; mitigation changes of about 1–3 pp). Abstract mentions 'without sacrificing code quality' but no quantitative code-quality measure is reported."}

{"eligibility": "include", "criterion": "IC", "side_list": "none", "reason": "Evaluates prompt interventions (accessibility request, English vs Portuguese prompts, Jetpack Compose vs XML layouts, Copilot) on LLM-generated Android UI code, with quantitative accessibility error counts from Accessibility Scanner.", "nf_outcomes_found": "Accessibility errors per generated screen (702 total across 288 screens; e.g., NReq 315 vs AccessReq 387; Compose yielded fewer errors than other layouts in Study 1; English prompts yielded 47 errors vs 270 for Portuguese in Study 2/3 comparison)."}

{"eligibility": "include", "criterion": "IC", "side_list": "none", "reason": "Evaluates prompt-context interventions (P1 minimal vs P2 summary) on LLM agents and reports quantitative SLOC, cyclomatic and cognitive complexity for generated microservices versus baselines.", "nf_outcomes_found": "Generated code shows about 15-40% lower cyclomatic and cognitive complexity than human baselines (CycC, CogC via SonarQube), with SLOC comparable or lower; efficiency reported as time, cost and tokens (RQ2)."}

{"eligibility": "include", "criterion": "IC", "side_list": "none", "reason": "Trains and evaluates direct vs. diff-based fine-tuned LLMs on Flutter/Dart edits, with a blinded judge's 1-5 code_quality ratings on LLM-generated code (Tables 7-8); code quality is a quantitative NF outcome.", "nf_outcomes_found": "Blinded LLM-judge code_quality scores (1-5) for LLM-generated code: direct 4.46 vs steps 3.96 (Rainbow-Pony) and 4.82 vs 4.52 (Qwen) among dart_pass rows; per-row judge win rates 4.8-9.2%. Dart analyze counts are released but not reported in the text."}

{"eligibility": "include", "criterion": "IC", "side_list": "none", "reason": "LLM-generated code is evaluated with a memory-augmented technique, and AlgoTune and KernelBench report quantitative speedups of generated code, an efficiency outcome.", "nf_outcomes_found": "AlgoTune routine speedups (average gain 7.90%, absolute baseline 461.5 vs 495.4 with memory) and KernelBench GPU-kernel speedups (average gain 16.89%, 2.49 vs 2.70), reported for LLM-evolved code. Search-speed ratios measure candidates evaluated, not code quality."}

{"eligibility": "exclude", "criterion": "IC3", "side_list": "adjacent", "reason": "Proposes an LLM-based code review and fix-suggestion tool, but reports no quantitative evaluation; the Results section is empty and the LLM mainly reviews and repairs human-written code.", "nf_outcomes_found": "none"}

{"eligibility": "exclude", "criterion": "EC5", "side_list": "correctness-only", "reason": "Code quality is measured only as pass@1 (functional correctness). Latency is inference overhead of the generator, not an NF property of the generated code, and detectability is not an NF outcome.", "nf_outcomes_found": "none"}

{"eligibility": "uncertain", "criterion": "IC3", "side_list": "correctness-only", "reason": "LLM-generated compiled operator code is evaluated mainly for agreement with the interpreter; reported time, cost and LLM-call savings concern the pipeline rather than the code's quality, so IC3 is unclear.", "nf_outcomes_found": "Per-query execution time of compiled operators (e.g., Exec in ms, up to 31x total speedup over interpretation), LLM calls and dollar cost savings in Palimpzest and SemBench; no code-level readability, complexity or security metrics."}

{"eligibility": "include", "criterion": "IC", "side_list": "none", "reason": "Proposes an RL fine-tuning technique (RLPF) on Qwen3-32B whose evaluated artifact is LLM-generated code, with quantitative runtime efficiency outcomes (CGRE, FBR, RBR) reported alongside correctness.", "nf_outcomes_found": "Relative efficiency (CGRE) rising from 8.1% to 38.6%; faster-than-baseline rate (FBR) 46.4% vs 8.2% base; reference-or-better (RBR) 31.1%; EffiBench-X execution time improvement +3.9% geometric mean, 57.9% win rate."}

{"eligibility": "include", "criterion": "IC", "side_list": "none", "reason": "SHADB applies an LLM-driven profile-guided loop to generate CUDA/HIP query kernels, and the paper reports quantitative execution-time (runtime efficiency) results for that generated code against baselines.", "nf_outcomes_found": "Warm execution time (ms) of LLM-synthesized SHADB-Opt/SHADB-Base CUDA kernels on SSB SF100 (e.g., 77.94 ms total, 7.4× faster than HeavyDB, 65× faster than DuckDB); also DRAM bandwidth utilization and synthesis cost ($126, 4.2 GPU-hours)."}

{"eligibility": "include", "criterion": "IC", "side_list": "none", "reason": "Evaluates ISO-grounded prompt enrichment (NL-rich, Structured) against a baseline on LLM-generated HumanEval code, with quantitative Pylint unreadability/smell densities and execution time as NF outcomes.", "nf_outcomes_found": "Unreadability density per 10 LOC (Performance 0.88→0.69 NL-rich; Error Handling 0.57→0.42; Code Smell 0.67→0.53; Readability 0.60→0.55), code-smell density (0.019→0.011), exception density (Error Handling 0.99→1.18), execution time, and STDEV of unreadability across prompt variations."}

{"eligibility": "include", "criterion": "IC", "side_list": "none", "reason": "Proposes an inference-time activation-steering technique (DuoSteer) applied to Llama and Qwen and measures vulnerability rate of their generated Python code via CodeQL, a quantitative security outcome, alongside correctness.", "nf_outcomes_found": "CodeQL-detected vulnerability rate (V) for generated code per CWE, e.g., CWE-502 falls from 64.7% to 0%, average −26.9% vulnerability reduction; joint C(1−V) score also reported."}

{"eligibility": "include", "criterion": "IC", "side_list": "none", "reason": "Evaluates guided decoding, Self-Refine and RAG on LLM code; Section 5.4 measures Semgrep code smell rates and syntax errors on LLM-generated full programs, and PHR is a supply-chain security outcome.", "nf_outcomes_found": "Package hallucination rate (security/supply-chain; e.g. Vanilla 30.0% overall micro PHR, RAG 18.1%, adversarial PHR up to +45 pp); Semgrep code smell count per sample and syntax error rate for full code generation (Figs. 2a-2b, e.g. Vanilla/Self-Refine highest smells in Rust)."}

{"eligibility": "exclude", "criterion": "EC5", "side_list": "correctness-only", "reason": "The only quantitative outcomes are LeetCode pass/success rates and strategy usage percentages; no runtime, memory, readability, or security of the generated code is measured, despite mentions of 'efficient' code.", "nf_outcomes_found": "none"}

{"eligibility": "exclude", "criterion": "IC3", "side_list": "context", "reason": "The paper trains a VLM critic whose F1 measures its own detection accuracy on injected UI violations. It does not change LLM code generation or report an NF quality outcome for LLM code.", "nf_out

{"eligibility": "include", "criterion": "IC", "side_list": "none", "reason": "Evaluates LLM coding agents under an iterative feedback and efficiency-prompting protocol, reporting quantitative runtime speedups (serial/parallel) for LLM-generated parallel code, an efficiency NF outcome.", "nf_outcomes_found": "Runtime speedup (serial/parallel) of LLM-generated parallel sorting, graph and search implementations in C++, Python and Julia; e.g., Sonnet 4.6 faster than serial in 7 of 15 language-algorithm combinations, GPT 5.4 none; Table IV graph runtimes, Table VI search runtimes. Correctness reported as co-outcome."}

{"eligibility": "exclude", "criterion": "IC3", "side_list": "correctness-only", "reason": "Reported quantitative outcomes are LOC/method/class counts, compilation rate, similarity to original code, and scenario intent. None measures readability, maintainability, efficiency, or security; structure claims are qualitative.", "nf_outcomes_found": "none (LOC/method/class counts, compile %, JPlag/CrystalBleu similarity, and scenario-intent rate are size, correctness-proxy, or similarity measures; resource cost concerns generation, not the code)"}

{"eligibility": "include", "criterion": "IC", "side_list": "none", "reason": "Evaluates six multi-agent LLM code-generation architectures (an intervention on LLM output) and reports quantitative RADON complexity outcomes (SLOC, CC, Halstead) for the generated HumanEval code.", "nf_outcomes_found": "Maintainability-related structural complexity of LLM-generated code: SLOC, cyclomatic complexity, and Halstead Volume/Difficulty/Effort per architecture. Heavy cluster has about 50–130% more complexity than the lean cluster (e.g., gpt-4o median SLOC 8 vs 5), with significant Friedman and Wilcoxon results."}

{"eligibility": "include", "criterion": "IC", "side_list": "none", "reason": "Proposes an RL and multi-turn refinement technique for Qwen-3-32B that generates CUDA kernels, with speedup (runtime efficiency) reported as a quantitative outcome for the generated code.", "nf_outcomes_found": "Geometric-mean speedup of LLM-generated CUDA kernels versus sequential code (e.g., CUDAPerf 11.02X vs Qwen-3-32B 6.2X on the CUDAPerf dataset, Table 1); also coefficient-of-variation stability penalty and ablations on speedup (Table 3)."}
